subject: standing versus sitting
title: What If You Never Sat Down Again?

scenes.text: What if you never sat down again? It sounds healthy. Your body might disagree.
The moment you stand, roughly half a litre to a full litre of blood pools in your legs and belly.
Standing burns barely more than sitting, about fifty-four extra calories across six hours.
Over a whole year, that adds up to roughly two and a half kilos, if you ate nothing extra.
But a twelve-year study of over seven thousand workers found standing jobs had about double the heart disease risk.
So standing all day just swaps one problem for another. Your body was built to keep changing position.

description:
What if you never sat down again? Standing pools roughly 500 to 1,000 mL of blood in the legs and abdomen, and a 2018 meta-analysis found standing burns about 0.15 kcal per minute more than sitting, about 54 kcal over six hours, or roughly 2.5 kg a year if intake stays the same.
A 12-year Ontario study of 7,320 workers found predominantly standing jobs carried about twice the heart disease risk of predominantly sitting jobs.
